models_evaluated: AI outcome prediction models trained on 46,631 ICU admissions (model type not specified)

links.outcome: AI versus clinician predictions of ICU mortality, length of stay, delirium and AKI on the same patients
links.effect: Retrospectively AI generally outperformed single clinicians, but aggregated predictions from 7 clinicians outperformed AI. Prospectively subspecialized physicians generally outperformed AI, while trainees and nurses underperformed AI. Both were poor at length-of-stay prediction.
links.quote: In the prospective setting, subspecialized physicians generally outperformed AI, whereas physicians in training and nurses generally underperformed AI.

screen.reason: Compares predictive performance of AI models against human clinicians (both retrospectively and prospectively collected clinician predictions), evaluating baseline model accuracy against human performance rather than testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
